hook: Heads, you win $150. Tails, you lose $100. Flip?
open_loop: Line 3 plants two promises: 'math says yes, big time' and 'why does your brain refuse?'; line 4 teases 'your brain secretly multiplies one side of this coin' without naming it. The brain half (named loss aversion + about 2x) lands in line 5 at ~15.0 s of ~43.1 s; the 'big time' math half carries to lines 7-9 (+$25 a flip, +$2,500 on average over 100 flips, under 2% chance of losing money) and is tied back to the brain by Benny's 'Wait... and I said no?' in the last ~10.8 s.
payoff: Your brain counts a loss about twice as heavily as a win (meta-analysis mean 1.955), so the $100 loss feels like about $195. But each flip pays +$25 on average: over 100 flips you are up $2,500 on average and lose money overall less than 2% of the time.

lines.text: Heads, you win $150. Tails, you lose $100. Flip?
lines.say: Heads, you win one fifty. Tails, you lose a hundred. Flip?
lines.ph: Heads, panalo ka ng $150. Tails, talo ka ng $100. I-flip mo?
lines.visual: Frame 0: Psychology Benny already holding a giant gold coin up to camera, one brow up (expression thinking, pose present). Green '+$150' pops left, red '-$100' pops right. No title card; first word at 0.0 s.

lines.text: Your hand froze, right? Most people say *no*.
lines.say: Your hand froze, right? Most people say no.
lines.visual: Close-up: Benny's own round hand hovers over the coin, trembles, then pulls back; he gulps (expression broke, pose worry). Hard cut to a red 'NO' stamp slamming down beside him.

lines.text: *Math* says yes, big time. So why does your brain refuse?
lines.say: Math says yes, big time. So why does your brain refuse?
lines.ph: Sabi ng *math*, oo, sobra pa. E bakit ayaw ng utak mo?
lines.visual: Split screen: calculator with a green check vs. Benny's pink brain with a red X. Benny looks from one to the other (expression thinking, pose think). A '?' pulses over the brain.

lines.text: Your brain secretly *multiplies* one side of this coin.
lines.say: Your brain secretly multiplies one side of this coin.
lines.ph: Kasi palihim na *pinalalaki* ng utak mo ang isang side ng coin.
lines.visual: Benny holds up the pink brain; a glowing 'x?' symbol hovers over the red '-$100' side of the coin, which starts to swell. Benny squints at it (expression thinking, pose point).

lines.text: *Loss aversion*: losses hurt about *twice* as much as wins.
lines.say: Loss aversion: losses hurt about twice as much as wins.
lines.ph: *Loss aversion*: mga *doble* ang sakit ng talo kaysa sa saya ng panalo.
lines.visual: Zoom punch on Benny, eyes wide (expression shocked, pose shock). 'LOSS AVERSION' stamp thuds, then a giant '~2x' slams onto the red side; a scale tips hard toward 'LOSS'. Small tag '150 studies' in the corner.

lines.text: So losing $100 feels like losing about $195.
lines.say: So losing a hundred feels like losing about a hundred ninety five dollars.
lines.ph: Kaya 'yung talo na $100, parang mga $195 ang sakit.
lines.visual: Two bars side by side: the red bar stretches up and relabels 'feels like -$195', towering over green 'real +$150'. Benny pockets the coin and slumps (expression broke, pose slump).

lines.text: But on average, each flip *pays you* $25.
lines.say: But on average, each flip pays you twenty five dollars.
lines.ph: Pero sa average, bawat flip, *kumikita ka* ng $25.
lines.visual: Benny pulls the coin back out with a smug 'alam ko na' half-lidded grin (expression smug, pose flex). A green '+$25' pops above the coin.

lines.say: Flip a hundred times: on average, you're up twenty five hundred dollars.
lines.ph: Mag-flip ka ng 100 beses: sa average, *ahead ka ng $2,500*.
lines.visual: Fast coin-flip montage; a '100 FLIPS' counter spins up while a green money counter races to '+$2,500'. Benny's jaw drops (expression shocked, pose run in place with excitement).

lines.text: Chance you lose money overall? Under *2%*. Wait... and I said *no*?
lines.say: Chance you lose money overall? Under two percent. Wait... and I said no?
lines.ph: Chance na talo ka sa dulo? Wala pang *2%*. Teka... tapos *umayaw* ako?
lines.visual: Pie chart: a huge green slice and a tiny red sliver labeled '<2%'. Benny stares at it, then at the pink brain in his hand, and mutters to himself (expression shocked, pose think) - Benny discovering his own bias. Then a gap-tooth half-grin.

lines.text: One flip's still 50/50. Heads, $150. Tails, lose $100. Do *you* flip?
lines.say: One flip's still fifty fifty. Heads, one fifty. Tails, lose a hundred. Do you flip?
lines.ph: Isang flip, 50/50 pa rin. Heads, $150. Tails, talo ng $100. I-flip mo ba?
lines.visual: Benny raises the coin to camera exactly like frame 0, same '+$150 / -$100' labels (seamless loop), hand hovering again but now with a gap-tooth grin (expression happy, pose point at viewer). Corner tag 'Not financial advice' stays on through this scene. Hard cut on 'flip?'.

disclaimer_on_screen: Not financial advice (corner tag, final scene; brain/decision thought experiment, not advice to gamble)

facts_used.claim: In the coin toss (win $150 / lose $100), most people decline.
Most people reject a 50/50 win $150 / lose $100 flip even though it is positive on average (corroborating).
Meta-analysis of 607 loss-aversion estimates from 150 articles ('150 studies' in script); mean coefficient 1.955, i.e. losses weigh about 2x an equal gain.
Losses tend to be treated as about twice as large as an equivalent gain; named 'loss aversion'.
The ~2:1 ratio varies by context (hence 'about twice', not 'exactly').
+$25 average per flip; a $100 loss 'feels like' about $195 at weight 1.955.
Over 100 fair flips: expected total +$2,500; chance of ending with a net loss 1.76% (<2%); each single flip is 50/50.

math_check: Average per flip = 0.5*150 - 0.5*100 = +$25. Felt loss = 1.955*100 = $195.50 -> 'about $195' (95% range 182.00-210.20, all > $150). 100 flips: expected total = 100*25 = +$2,500. With h heads, total = 150h - 100(100-h) = 250h - 10,000, which is < 0 iff h <= 39 (h = 40 is exactly break-even); P(h <= 39 | n=100, p=0.5) = 0.017600 = 1.76% < 2%. Re-computed in .venv python.
